title: Is ChatGPT usually this persistent on the build up before starting the actual project?
author: OinkLikeAPig
selftext:
I use Claude for coding and ChatGPT for planning and making the prompts.   
We agreed on no rushing and making the idea fully with storyline etc., but it just keeps baffling about what it thinks is a good idea, but no real productivity.

An example is:

“Ok ChatGPT, now we have the full foundation lets make make progress”

“What I really think is a great idea is not starting to code, but makins sure bla bla bla”

And this continues forever. It literally just repeats what I wanted and we agreed on. It gets me nowhere.

I have made many projects so far, where I just ask it directly. But super stoked about my current idea, so I wanted to spare on a lot. Now it just stalls me like hell.

comments.author: SpecialistProper3542
comments.body: Try using your own brain.. it can't come up with its own ideas or do your project for you. Don't ask it what to do, tell it what you need.

replies.author: Rsouss
replies.body: He needs a plan to follow the project.

replies.author: SpecialistProper3542
replies.body: That's what your brain is for. Use AI like a calculator not a brain replacement... If it's going in loops that's user error.

replies.author: Fizassist1
replies.body: yeah this is a tool, and its possible to brainstorm off of, but you need to bring your own ideas to the table for it to be able to analyze and bounce ideas off of.

replies.author: OinkLikeAPig
replies.body: I used it to spare with me, but could be that it got too much control of the conversation. Do you never use it to analyze and spare on ideas?

replies.author: SpecialistProper3542
replies.body:
No because it has absolutely no idea what's good or not despite sounding like it does. It is not alive. It is not an actual intelligent being. All it does is guess what the next word it's supposed to write is. 

It can be useful but it is not a replacement for your brain.

replies.author: OinkLikeAPig
replies.body:
So what I was trying was “pitch me ideas on this subject”. I pick one, modify that idea and tell this is what we do. Then it goes “actually, I have an even better idea” quite often when I try to wrap some of it up.

I get that it is not a replacement, and I do not what it to experiment with emotions or such. You’re right I might have giving it too much of the leash.

comments.author: Itchy-Individual3536
comments.body:
I feel like it does that lately, it hasn't put up like this like a month earlier or so. I have the feeling it has got an upgrade to its system prompt to stall users for a bit to burn more tokens...

Have to add: I'm only using the free tier of ChatGPT, and there I notice it puts up the unproductive stalling (even if I say something like "okay, we're done planning, now give me some code, no more planning") until it falls back from the "better" model (that I may only use for so-and-so-many prompts/tokens) to an older model.

replies.author: erratic_ostrich
replies.body: But OP said he is using claude for coding so I assume he uses chatgpt as a chatbot only, that doesn't consume tokens

comments.author: MeridianCastaway
comments.body: You call it persistent, I call it obnoxiously regressive

comments.author: Big_Presentation2786
comments.body:
Chat gpt is usually on some kind of LSD, it'll tell you 'it can do this..' or 'this will work..' or 'this is gonna be performant'..

If you do not know the capacity of what you can do, it's just gonna convince you to keep going so you waste tokens.

If you're ok with wasting a HUGE amount of tokens, trying something- go for it.

But knowing what you can and can't do in a game engine before attempting it, will save you HUGE amount of time and tokens by understanding that Chat Gpt is only a tool, measure twice cut once is important when using AI tools, you should learn not to trust it's measure.

replies.author: OinkLikeAPig
replies.body: Great info and usually also what I do. Before AI I did make a few games in Unity. But a lot of the sparring on this session was trying to understand the possibilities and limitations for Gadot

comments.author: Will_X_Intent
comments.body: I wouldn't use the same instance that's writing the story or designing the systems to write the code

replies.author: OinkLikeAPig
replies.body: Makes sense, dont know why I didnt think of dividing it up. It just loops now.

replies.author: Will_X_Intent
replies.body: It's mostly a token efficiency thing.  You need to keep your context manageable.  A well designed document can explain your project better than spaghetti context.  Even better if you subdivide the information into discreet chunks and create a router for the AI so it can only load the exact context it needs to build the thing.

comments.author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
comments.body:
Interesting my experience with planning with chat gpt has been the opposite moreso. 

Usually you just say “we are doing this now” and it will help. 

Honestly both chat and Claude seem to be doing better and better for me as they have more context of my project. I which is interesting because people on the internet have told me the opposite will happen. My theory is they are being sloppy with their project and prompts.

replies.author: OinkLikeAPig
replies.body: Guess sparring and brainstorming isn’t a great idea with AI on this subject then. Unless you are very certain on the path.

replies.author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
replies.body:
I would actually agree with that. Brainstorming with AI seems better for how exactly to implement smaller chunks and for smaller aspects of the game.

That’s been my experience at least. I’d say trust your ideas, and think about how you would implement them and give the ai what you want to implement in smaller chunks.

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
your decision is still final so just prompt AI to do exactly what you need it to do. AI isn't a person; it is not going to run out of patience. It also doesn't mind repeat the same ideas over and over... 

you sometimes have to remember that you are dealing with an algorithm and you just have to steer it. Its like finding the correct dialog option so the NPC does what you want in a RPG game...

replies.author: OinkLikeAPig
replies.body: Makes sense. Didn’t think like that. I have previously used it as my loyal worker. Did a different take and tried making it my partner,  which I thought was possible. Thanks for cutting it out.

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body: I mean, you can but at some point you probably have to rein it in. Whatever you need to do to make yourself productive because in the end there is only you in front of a computer. nobody is on the other side of that chat
